quote: "The Commission shall, by means of an implementing act, make provisions on the establishment of a scientific panel of independent experts (the ‘scientific panel’) intended to support the enforcement activities under this Regulation. That implementing act shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 98(2)."
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: The scientific panel must advise and support the AI Office on GPAI implementation and enforcement, including systemic-risk alerts, evaluation tools, classification advice, templates and support to market surveillance and safeguard procedures.
quote: "The scientific panel shall advise and support the AI Office, in particular with regard to the following tasks:"
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: Scientific-panel experts must act impartially and objectively, keep information confidential, avoid instructions, publish declarations of interests, and the AI Office must manage conflicts; implementing acts must set alert and assistance procedures.
quote: "The experts on the scientific panel shall perform their tasks with impartiality and objectivity, and shall ensure the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities. They shall neither seek nor take instructions from anyone when exercising their tasks under paragraph 3. Each expert shall draw up"
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: Member States may call on scientific-panel experts for enforcement support, may be required to pay fees set in the Article 68 implementing act, and the Commission must facilitate timely, organised access to experts.
quote: "Member States may call upon experts of the scientific panel to support their enforcement activities under this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: Each Member State must establish or designate at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority, which must exercise powers independently, impartially and without bias.
quote: "Each Member State shall establish or designate as national competent authorities at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation. Those national competent authorities shall exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias so as to safeguard the objectivity of their activities and"
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: Member States must communicate authority identities and tasks and later changes to the Commission, publish contact information by 2 August 2025, designate a single point of contact and notify it, and the Commission must publish the list.
quote: "Member States shall communicate to the Commission the identity of the notifying authorities and the market surveillance authorities and the tasks of those authorities, as well as any subsequent changes thereto. Member States shall make publicly available information on how competent authorities and single points of contact can be contacted, through electronic"
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: Member States must resource national competent authorities, assess resources annually, ensure adequate cybersecurity and confidentiality, and report resource status to the Commission every two years from 2 August 2025 for Board discussion.
quote: "Member States shall ensure that their national competent authorities are provided with adequate technical, financial and human resources, and with infrastructure to fulfil their tasks effectively under this Regulation. In particular, the national competent authorities shall have a sufficient number of personnel permanently available whose competences and expertise shall include an in-depth"
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: The Commission must facilitate exchanges among national competent authorities, national authorities may provide guidance and consult other Union-law authorities where relevant, and the EDPS supervises Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
quote: "The Commission shall facilitate the exchange of experience between national competent authorities."
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: The Commission, with Member States, must set up and maintain the EU database for Annex III high-risk AI systems and certain non-high-risk registrations.
quote: "The Commission shall, in collaboration with the Member States, set up and maintain an EU database containing information referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article concerning high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)"
legal_practice_note: Legal AI vendors and public-authority deployers may appear in this public EU database.

summary: Providers or authorised representatives must enter Annex VIII Sections A and B data into the EU database for covered high-risk and non-high-risk systems.
quote: "The data listed in Sections A and B of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the provider or, where applicable, by the authorised representative."
legal_practice_note: A legal-AI vendor providing an Annex III high-risk system would be responsible for this registration data.

summary: Public-authority deployers, or those acting for them, must enter Annex VIII Section C data into the EU database under Article 49.
quote: "The data listed in Section C of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the deployer who is, or who acts on behalf of, a public authority, agency or body"
legal_practice_note: Courts and public legal bodies deploying high-risk AI are public-authority deployers for this registration duty.

summary: The EU database must make most Article 49 registration information public, user-friendly, navigable and machine-readable, while real-world testing data remains restricted unless consent is given.
quote: "the information contained in the EU database registered in accordance with Article 49 shall be accessible and publicly available in a user-friendly manner"
legal_practice_note: Public availability may identify registered legal-sector high-risk systems and public deployments.

summary: The EU database may contain personal data only as necessary for collecting and processing information under the Regulation.
quote: "The EU database shall contain personal data only in so far as necessary for collecting and processing information in accordance with this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: Registration may include contact details for persons representing a provider or deployer.

summary: The Commission is controller of the EU database and must provide technical and administrative support and ensure accessibility requirements are met.
quote: "The Commission shall be the controller of the EU database. It shall make available to providers, prospective providers and deployers adequate technical and administrative support."
legal_practice_note: This supports operators, including legal-sector providers and deployers, that must use the database.

summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems must establish, document and operate a proportionate post-market monitoring system throughout the system lifetime.
quote: "Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system in a manner that is proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks of the high-risk AI system."
legal_practice_note: A vendor of a high-risk legal AI system must monitor performance and compliance after market placement.

summary: The post-market monitoring system must be based on a plan included in technical documentation, and the Commission must set a plan template by implementing act.
quote: "The post-market monitoring system shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan. The post-market monitoring plan shall be part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV."
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI vendors whose systems are high-risk need this documented monitoring plan.

summary: Providers of high-risk systems already covered by listed harmonisation or financial-services monitoring regimes may integrate AI Act monitoring elements into existing systems when protection is equivalent.
quote: "providers shall have a choice of integrating, as appropriate, the necessary elements described in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 using the template referred in paragraph 3 into systems and plans already existing under that legislation"
legal_practice_note: This mainly affects regulated product and financial-services providers rather than ordinary legal deployers.

summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market must report serious incidents to the market surveillance authority where the incident occurred.
quote: "Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred."
legal_practice_note: A provider of high-risk legal AI would report qualifying serious incidents to the relevant market surveillance authority.

summary: The serious-incident report must be made immediately after a causal link or reasonable likelihood is established and no later than 15 days after awareness.
quote: "not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware of the serious incident"
legal_practice_note: This 15-day deadline matters to legal-AI vendors once a serious incident is known.

summary: For widespread infringements and serious incidents under Article 3(49)(b), the provider must report immediately and within two days of awareness.
quote: "the report referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall be provided immediately, and not later than two days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer becomes aware of that incident"
legal_practice_note: The two-day accelerated report can affect providers when high-risk legal AI creates widespread infringement-type incidents.

summary: In the event of a death, the report must be made immediately once causality is established or suspected and no later than 10 days after awareness.
quote: "in the event of the death of a person, the report shall be provided immediately after the provider or the deployer has established, or as soon as it suspects, a causal relationship"
legal_practice_note: This death-related deadline is unlikely in ordinary legal AI but is part of high-risk incident reporting.

summary: Where timely reporting requires it, the provider or deployer may file an incomplete initial report followed by a complete report.
quote: "the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, may submit an initial report that is incomplete, followed by a complete report"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI operators may use this staged reporting mechanism when incident facts are incomplete.

summary: After reporting, the provider must investigate without delay, assess risk, take corrective action, cooperate with authorities and avoid altering the system before informing them.
quote: "the provider shall, without delay, perform the necessary investigations in relation to the serious incident and the AI system concerned"
legal_practice_note: A legal-AI provider subject to serious-incident reporting must also investigate and coordinate with authorities.

summary: Market surveillance authorities must inform fundamental-rights authorities for Article 3(49)(c) incidents and act within seven days; the Commission must issue and assess guidance.
quote: "The market surveillance authority shall take appropriate measures, as provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, within seven days from the date it received the notification"
legal_practice_note: Incidents affecting fundamental rights in legal AI may trigger fast authority action and guidance.

summary: For Annex III systems with equivalent Union reporting duties, and for medical-device or IVD safety-component systems, serious-incident notification is limited to Article 3(49)(c) incidents.
quote: "the notification of serious incidents shall be limited to those referred to in Article 3, point (49)(c)"
legal_practice_note: This primarily affects sector-regulated providers, not most legal-sector AI systems.

summary: National competent authorities must immediately notify the Commission of every serious incident, whether or not they have acted on it.
quote: "National competent authorities shall immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident, whether or not they have taken action on it"
legal_practice_note: This is an authority reporting duty following incidents involving high-risk systems.

summary: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies to AI systems, with economic-operator and product references read to include AI Act operators and systems.
quote: "Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to AI systems covered by this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: Market surveillance powers can reach legal-AI operators whose systems fall within the Regulation.

summary: Market surveillance authorities must report annually to the Commission and competition authorities on competition-relevant findings, prohibited practices and measures taken.
quote: "the market surveillance authorities shall report annually to the Commission and relevant national competition authorities any information identified in the course of market surveillance activities"
legal_practice_note: This is an authority reporting channel, not a direct law-firm obligation.

summary: For product-related high-risk AI under Annex I Section A, the sectoral market surveillance authority is responsible unless Member States designate another coordinated authority; equivalent sectoral procedures may apply.
quote: "the market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation shall be the authority responsible for market surveillance activities designated under those legal acts"
legal_practice_note: This primarily allocates authority responsibility for regulated product sectors.

summary: Market surveillance authorities may exercise specified Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 powers remotely when appropriate for effective AI Act enforcement.
quote: "market surveillance authorities may exercise the powers referred to in Article 14(4), points (d) and (j), of that Regulation remotely, as appropriate"
legal_practice_note: Remote inspection powers may affect providers and deployers under investigation.

summary: For high-risk AI used by regulated financial institutions in direct connection with financial services, the relevant financial supervisor is the market surveillance authority unless another coordinated authority is identified.
quote: "the market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation shall be the relevant national authority responsible for the financial supervision of those institutions"
legal_practice_note: This may matter to in-house legal teams at financial institutions using high-risk AI.

summary: For specified biometric, law-enforcement, migration and justice high-risk systems, Member States must designate data-protection or equivalent authorities and must not interfere with judicial independence.
quote: "Market surveillance activities shall in no way affect the independence of judicial authorities, or otherwise interfere with their activities when acting in their judicial capacity."
legal_practice_note: This directly concerns high-risk AI used in justice and democratic-process contexts, including courts.

summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor acts as market surveillance authority for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, except for the CJEU acting judicially.
quote: "the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as their market surveillance authority, except in relation to the Court of Justice of the European Union acting in its judicial capacity"
legal_practice_note: This matters to EU institutions deploying AI and preserves the Court of Justice judicial carve-out.

summary: Member States must facilitate coordination among relevant authorities, and market surveillance authorities and the Commission may conduct joint compliance, investigation, awareness or guidance activities with AI Office support.
quote: "Market surveillance authorities and the Commission shall be able to propose joint activities, including joint investigations"
legal_practice_note: Joint investigations could involve cross-border legal-AI providers or public-sector deployers.

summary: Providers must give market surveillance authorities full access to documentation and relevant training, validation and testing datasets where necessary for enforcement tasks.
quote: "the market surveillance authorities shall be granted full access by providers to the documentation as well as the training, validation and testing data sets used for the development of high-risk AI systems"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI vendors of high-risk systems may have to provide documentation and datasets to authorities.

summary: Market surveillance authorities may access high-risk AI source code only on a reasoned request when needed for conformity assessment and other testing or documentation checks are insufficient.
quote: "Market surveillance authorities shall be granted access to the source code of the high-risk AI system upon a reasoned request"
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal-AI providers could face source-code access requests under the Article 74 conditions.

summary: Information or documentation obtained by market surveillance authorities under Article 74 must be treated under the Article 78 confidentiality duties.
quote: "Any information or documentation obtained by market surveillance authorities shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78."
legal_practice_note: This protects confidential material disclosed by legal-AI providers or deployers during supervision.

summary: Where an AI system is based on a general-purpose AI model and both are developed by the same provider, the AI Office can monitor and supervise compliance using market-surveillance powers.
quote: "the AI Office shall have powers to monitor and supervise compliance of that AI system with obligations under this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: This may reach integrated legal AI systems built on a provider’s own general-purpose model.

summary: Market surveillance authorities investigating high-risk systems may request AI Office enforcement of access to general-purpose model information; the AI Office must supply relevant information within 30 days.
quote: "the AI Office shall supply to the applicant authority without delay, and in any event within 30 days, any information that the AI Office considers to be relevant"
legal_practice_note: This can affect high-risk legal AI that depends on a GPAI model controlled outside the deployer investigation.

summary: Market surveillance authorities have competence and powers to ensure that testing in real-world conditions complies with the Regulation, including sandbox-supervised testing.
quote: "Market surveillance authorities shall have competences and powers to ensure that testing in real world conditions is in accordance with this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: Providers or prospective providers testing high-risk legal AI may be supervised under these powers.

summary: If serious incidents or unmet testing conditions arise, a market surveillance authority may suspend or terminate testing or require modifications by providers and deployers.
quote: "it may take either of the following decisions on its territory, as appropriate:"
legal_practice_note: Real-world testing of high-risk legal AI could be stopped or changed by authorities.

summary: Authority decisions or objections on real-world testing must state reasons and challenge routes, and grounds must be communicated to other Member State authorities when applicable.
quote: "the decision or the objection shall indicate the grounds therefor and how the provider or prospective provider can challenge the decision or objection"
legal_practice_note: This is a procedural protection for supervised real-world testing.

summary: Fundamental-rights supervisory or enforcement authorities may request and access AI Act documentation for Annex III high-risk systems when needed for their mandates.
quote: "shall have the power to request and access any documentation created or maintained under this Regulation in accessible language and format"
legal_practice_note: Authorities protecting fundamental rights may access documentation for high-risk AI used in justice and other legal contexts.

summary: Member States must identify, publish, notify and keep updated the list of authorities and bodies empowered under Article 77(1).
quote: "each Member State shall identify the public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 and make a list of them publicly available"
legal_practice_note: The list identifies which fundamental-rights authorities can request documents about high-risk legal AI.

summary: If documentation is insufficient to assess a fundamental-rights infringement, the relevant public authority may request testing, and the market surveillance authority must organise it with close involvement.
quote: "the public authority or body referred to in paragraph 1 may make a reasoned request to the market surveillance authority, to organise testing of the high-risk AI system"
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal AI affecting fundamental rights may be tested at the request of rights authorities.

summary: Authorities, notified bodies and others involved in applying the Regulation must respect confidentiality of information and data obtained in their tasks.
quote: "shall, in accordance with Union or national law, respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities"
legal_practice_note: This protects trade secrets, source code and confidential business information disclosed by legal-AI actors.

summary: Authorities must request only strictly necessary data, use cybersecurity measures and delete collected data when no longer needed under applicable law.
quote: "The authorities involved in the application of this Regulation pursuant to paragraph 1 shall request only data that is strictly necessary"
legal_practice_note: This limits regulatory data requests to legal-AI providers and deployers and protects sensitive files.

summary: Confidential information exchanged between authorities cannot be disclosed without prior consultation where specified Annex III law-enforcement, border, immigration or asylum uses could jeopardise security interests.
quote: "information exchanged on a confidential basis between the national competent authorities or between national competent authorities and the Commission shall not be disclosed without prior consultation"
legal_practice_note: This is most relevant to public-sector legal and enforcement deployments, not ordinary law-firm AI.

summary: The Commission and Member States may exchange confidential information with third-country regulators under relevant agreements and adequate confidentiality arrangements.
quote: "The Commission and Member States may exchange, where necessary and in accordance with relevant provisions of international and trade agreements, confidential information with regulatory authorities of third countries"
legal_practice_note: This is an authority-to-authority confidentiality rule.

summary: AI systems presenting risk are treated as products presenting risk, and authorities must evaluate suspected risky systems against AI Act requirements and obligations.
quote: "AI systems presenting a risk shall be understood as a ‘product presenting a risk’ as defined in Article 3, point 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI systems presenting health, safety or fundamental-rights risk can trigger this evaluation process.

summary: When non-compliance is found, the market surveillance authority must require the operator to correct, withdraw or recall the AI system within the prescribed period, capped by the shorter 15-working-day rule where applicable.
quote: "it shall without undue delay require the relevant operator to take all appropriate corrective actions to bring the AI system into compliance, to withdraw the AI system from the market, or to recall it"
legal_practice_note: Providers or deployers of legal AI may have to take corrective action after an authority evaluation.

summary: Where non-compliance is not limited nationally, authorities must inform the Commission and other Member States, and operators must correct all affected Union-market systems.
quote: "it shall inform the Commission and the other Member States without undue delay of the results of the evaluation and of the actions which it has required the operator to take"
legal_practice_note: Cross-border legal-AI offerings may face Union-wide corrective action.

summary: If an operator does not take adequate corrective action, the market surveillance authority must take provisional measures to prohibit, restrict, withdraw or recall the system and notify others.
quote: "the market surveillance authority shall take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict the AI system’s being made available on its national market or put into service"
legal_practice_note: A non-compliant legal-AI system could be restricted, withdrawn or recalled under this procedure.

summary: Other market surveillance authorities must report measures, information and objections; if no objection is raised within the applicable period, the provisional measure is deemed justified.
quote: "Where, within three months of receipt of the notification referred to in paragraph 5 of this Article, no objection has been raised"
legal_practice_note: This determines whether national measures against legal-AI systems become accepted across authorities.

summary: Market surveillance authorities must evaluate AI systems classified by providers as non-high-risk when they have sufficient reason to consider the system is actually high-risk.
quote: "a market surveillance authority has sufficient reason to consider that an AI system classified by the provider as non-high-risk pursuant to Article 6(3) is indeed high-risk"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI vendors relying on the Article 6(3) non-high-risk route may be challenged by authorities.

summary: If the system is found high-risk, the provider must take necessary action to meet AI Act high-risk requirements and obligations and take corrective action within the prescribed period.
quote: "it shall without undue delay require the relevant provider to take all necessary actions to bring the AI system into compliance with the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: A legal-AI provider may have to recode, document or assess a system after misclassification is found.

summary: Providers that fail to bring a reclassified high-risk system into compliance within the prescribed period are subject to fines and must correct all affected Union-market systems.
quote: "the provider shall be subject to fines in accordance with Article 99"
legal_practice_note: Misclassification of legal-sector high-risk AI may expose the provider to Article 99 fines.

summary: Intentional misclassification to circumvent Chapter III Section 2 triggers Article 99 fines, and authorities may use EU database information for checks.
quote: "the AI system was misclassified by the provider as non-high-risk in order to circumvent the application of requirements in Chapter III, Section 2"
legal_practice_note: This is directly relevant to legal-AI providers claiming an Annex III system is non-high-risk.

summary: When objections are raised or the Commission considers a national measure contrary to Union law, the Commission must consult, evaluate and decide whether the measure is justified within the applicable deadline.
quote: "the Commission shall without undue delay enter into consultation with the market surveillance authority of the relevant Member State and the operator or operators, and shall evaluate the national measure"
legal_practice_note: This can determine Union-wide treatment of measures against legal-AI systems.

summary: If the Commission finds a national measure justified, all Member States must take appropriate restrictive measures; if unjustified, the Member State must withdraw it.
quote: "all Member States shall ensure that they take appropriate restrictive measures in respect of the AI system concerned"
legal_practice_note: A justified safeguard decision could restrict a legal-AI system across Member States.

summary: If justified non-compliance is due to harmonised standard or common specification shortcomings, the Commission must use the Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 procedure.
quote: "the Commission shall apply the procedure provided for in Article 11 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012"
legal_practice_note: This concerns standards governance rather than a direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Even if a high-risk AI system complies with the Regulation, authorities must require measures if it still risks health, safety, fundamental rights or public interests.
quote: "although a high-risk AI system complies with this Regulation, it nevertheless presents a risk to the health or safety of persons, to fundamental rights"
legal_practice_note: A formally compliant high-risk legal-AI system may still be subject to corrective measures if it presents fundamental-rights risk.

summary: The provider or other relevant operator must ensure corrective action is taken for all affected Union-market systems within the authority-prescribed timeline.
quote: "The provider or other relevant operator shall ensure that corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems concerned"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI providers or operators may need to correct all affected systems, not only one deployment.

summary: Member States must inform the Commission and other Member States of compliant-risk findings, and the Commission must consult, evaluate, decide and communicate whether measures are justified.
quote: "The Commission shall without undue delay enter into consultation with the Member States concerned and the relevant operators, and shall evaluate the national measures taken."
legal_practice_note: This procedure can affect high-risk legal-AI systems presenting risks despite formal compliance.

summary: When formal non-compliance is found, including CE marking, EU declaration, database registration, authorised-representative or technical-documentation failures, the authority must require the provider to end it.
quote: "it shall require the relevant provider to put an end to the non-compliance concerned, within a period it may prescribe"
legal_practice_note: High-risk legal-AI providers can be required to fix formal compliance failures.

summary: If formal non-compliance persists, the authority must take proportionate measures to restrict, prohibit, recall or withdraw the high-risk AI system without delay.
quote: "the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned shall take appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the high-risk AI system being made available on the market"
legal_practice_note: Persistent formal failures can remove a high-risk legal-AI system from the market.

summary: The Commission must designate one or more Union AI testing support structures to perform AI-related tasks under Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
quote: "The Commission shall designate one or more Union AI testing support structures to perform the tasks listed under Article 21(6) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020"
legal_practice_note: This creates institutional testing support rather than a direct legal-sector duty.

summary: Union AI testing support structures must provide independent technical or scientific advice when requested by the Board, Commission or market surveillance authorities.
quote: "Union AI testing support structures shall also provide independent technical or scientific advice at the request of the Board, the Commission, or of market surveillance authorities."
legal_practice_note: This supports enforcement and governance bodies.

summary: Any natural or legal person with grounds to consider there has been an AI Act infringement may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority.
quote: "any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the provisions of this Regulation may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority"
legal_practice_note: Clients, employees, litigants or organisations may complain about AI Act infringements affecting legal contexts.

summary: Market surveillance authorities must take such complaints into account for market-surveillance activities and handle them through dedicated procedures.
quote: "such complaints shall be taken into account for the purpose of conducting market surveillance activities, and shall be handled in line with the dedicated procedures"
legal_practice_note: Complaints about legal-AI systems can feed into market surveillance procedures.

summary: Affected persons subject to certain deployer decisions based on Annex III high-risk AI outputs with legal or similarly significant effects have a right to clear and meaningful explanations.
quote: "shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure"
legal_practice_note: This is directly relevant where legal or public-authority decisions use high-risk AI outputs.

summary: The explanation right does not apply where Union or national law, in compliance with Union law, provides exceptions or restrictions to that obligation.
quote: "Paragraph 1 shall not apply to the use of AI systems for which exceptions from, or restrictions to, the obligation under that paragraph follow from Union or national law"
legal_practice_note: Legal decision-making contexts may have Union or national-law limits on explanations.

summary: Article 86 applies only to the extent the same explanation right is not otherwise provided under Union law.
quote: "This Article shall apply only to the extent that the right referred to in paragraph 1 is not otherwise provided for under Union law."
legal_practice_note: The Article 86 right coexists with other Union-law explanation or information rights.

summary: The EU whistleblower directive applies to reporting AI Act infringements and protecting persons who report them.
quote: "Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements."
legal_practice_note: Personnel at legal organisations or vendors reporting AI Act infringements may receive whistleblower protections.

summary: The Commission has exclusive power to supervise and enforce Chapter V for GPAI models and entrusts implementation to the AI Office, subject to procedural guarantees.
quote: "The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V, taking into account the procedural guarantees under Article 94."
legal_practice_note: GPAI model providers serving legal-AI vendors are supervised at Union level.

summary: Market surveillance authorities may request the Commission to use Section 5 powers where necessary and proportionate for their AI Act tasks.
quote: "market surveillance authorities may request the Commission to exercise the powers laid down in this Section"
legal_practice_note: A national investigation of legal AI using GPAI may lead to a Commission enforcement request.

summary: The AI Office may take necessary monitoring actions for effective implementation and compliance by GPAI model providers, including adherence to approved codes of practice.
quote: "the AI Office may take the necessary actions to monitor the effective implementation and compliance with this Regulation by providers of general-purpose AI models"
legal_practice_note: Monitoring of GPAI model providers can affect models incorporated into legal AI products.

summary: Downstream providers have the right to lodge a reasoned complaint alleging GPAI-provider infringement, with contact, facts, provisions and relevant supporting information.
quote: "Downstream providers shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: A legal-AI vendor integrating a GPAI model may complain about the model provider.

summary: The scientific panel may provide a qualified alert to the AI Office when it suspects a GPAI model poses Union-level concrete identifiable risk or meets systemic-risk conditions.
quote: "The scientific panel may provide a qualified alert to the AI Office where it has reason to suspect"
legal_practice_note: A widely used GPAI model in legal products could be subject to systemic-risk alert processes.

summary: After a qualified alert, the Commission through the AI Office may exercise Section 5 powers and must inform the Board of Article 91 to 94 measures.
quote: "the Commission, through the AI Office and after having informed the Board, may exercise the powers laid down in this Section"
legal_practice_note: This can trigger documentation, access or mitigation steps for GPAI models used in legal AI.

summary: A qualified alert must be reasoned and include the provider contact point, facts, reasons and any other relevant information gathered by the scientific panel.
quote: "A qualified alert shall be duly reasoned and indicate at least"
legal_practice_note: This is a scientific panel procedural content requirement.

summary: The Commission may require a GPAI model provider to provide Article 53 and 55 documentation or other information needed to assess compliance.
quote: "The Commission may request the provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned to provide the documentation drawn up by the provider in accordance with Articles 53 and 55"
legal_practice_note: GPAI providers that supply models for legal AI may have to produce compliance documentation.

summary: Requests for GPAI information must state legal basis, purpose, required information, response period and Article 101 fines for incorrect, incomplete or misleading information.
quote: "The request for information shall state the legal basis and the purpose of the request, specify what information is required, set a period within which the information is to be provided"
legal_practice_note: This is a procedural safeguard around Commission requests to GPAI providers.

summary: The GPAI model provider or representative must supply requested information, with authorised persons or lawyers able to respond while clients remain responsible for completeness and accuracy.
quote: "The provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned, or its representative shall supply the information requested."
legal_practice_note: Lawyers can supply information for clients, but GPAI-provider clients remain responsible if it is incomplete, incorrect or misleading.

summary: The AI Office may evaluate GPAI models to assess provider compliance where Article 91 information is insufficient or to investigate Union-level systemic risks.
quote: "The AI Office, after consulting the Board, may conduct evaluations of the general-purpose AI model concerned"
legal_practice_note: Systemic GPAI models used in legal AI may be evaluated by the AI Office.

summary: The Commission may appoint independent experts and request model access through APIs or other technical means, including source code, for evaluations.
quote: "the Commission may request access to the general-purpose AI model concerned through APIs or further appropriate technical means and tools, including source code"
legal_practice_note: GPAI providers behind legal-AI tooling may face technical access requests for model evaluation.

summary: A model-access request must state legal basis, purpose, reasons, response period and Article 101 fines for failure to provide access.
quote: "The request for access shall state the legal basis, the purpose and reasons of the request and set the period within which the access is to be provided"
legal_practice_note: This is a procedural safeguard around model access requests.

summary: The GPAI model provider or its representative must provide the access requested for Commission or AI Office evaluations.
quote: "The providers of the general-purpose AI model concerned or its representative shall supply the information requested."
legal_practice_note: GPAI providers used by legal AI systems may need to provide technical access for evaluations.

summary: Where necessary and appropriate, the Commission may request GPAI providers to comply with Articles 53 and 54, mitigate systemic risk, or restrict, withdraw or recall the model.
quote: "Where necessary and appropriate, the Commission may request providers to:"
legal_practice_note: Models integrated into legal AI could be subject to compliance, mitigation or market-restriction measures.

summary: If a systemic-risk GPAI provider offers mitigation commitments during structured dialogue, the Commission may make them binding and close further action grounds.
quote: "the Commission may, by decision, make those commitments binding and declare that there are no further grounds for action"
legal_practice_note: This is a GPAI enforcement settlement-style mechanism.

summary: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies to GPAI providers, subject to more specific procedural rights in the AI Act.
quote: "Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the providers of the general-purpose AI model"
legal_practice_note: GPAI providers serving legal AI retain procedural rights in Commission enforcement.

summary: The AI Office and Member States must encourage and facilitate codes of conduct for voluntary application of some or all Chapter III Section 2 requirements to non-high-risk AI systems.
quote: "shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of conduct, including related governance mechanisms"
legal_practice_note: Legal organisations using non-high-risk AI may be covered by voluntary codes modeled on high-risk requirements.

summary: The AI Office and Member States must facilitate codes on voluntary specific requirements for all AI systems, including ethics, environmental sustainability, AI literacy, inclusive design and vulnerable groups.
quote: "shall facilitate the drawing up of codes of conduct concerning the voluntary application, including by deployers, of specific requirements to all AI systems"
legal_practice_note: This can reach law firms, legal departments and courts as deployers through voluntary AI-use commitments.

summary: Codes of conduct may be drawn up by providers, deployers or their organisations with stakeholders, and the AI Office and Member States must consider SME and startup interests.
quote: "Codes of conduct may be drawn up by individual providers or deployers of AI systems or by organisations representing them or by both"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI vendors and legal deployers may participate in sector codes of conduct.

summary: The Commission must develop practical implementation guidelines on high-risk requirements, prohibited practices, substantial modification, transparency, harmonisation-law relationships and the AI-system definition.
quote: "The Commission shall develop guidelines on the practical implementation of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Commission guidance will shape how legal-AI providers and deployers understand their obligations.

summary: The Commission must update previously adopted guidelines when needed, on request from Member States or the AI Office or on its own initiative.
quote: "the Commission shall update guidelines previously adopted when deemed necessary"
legal_practice_note: Updates may change interpretive guidance relevant to legal-sector AI compliance.

summary: The Commission receives delegated-act powers under listed provisions, subject to Article 97 conditions and a five-year delegation period starting 1 August 2024.
quote: "The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article."
legal_practice_note: Delegated acts may later alter technical obligations affecting legal-AI providers or deployers.

summary: The Commission must report on delegated powers before the five-year period ends, and delegation extends tacitly unless Parliament or Council opposes.
quote: "The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period."
legal_practice_note: This is institutional oversight of the Act’s delegated powers.

summary: Delegated acts enter into force only if Parliament and Council do not object within the three-month period, extendable by three months.
quote: "shall enter into force only if no objection has been expressed by either the European Parliament or the Council within a period of three months"
legal_practice_note: This is the institutional control mechanism for delegated changes.

summary: The Commission is assisted by a Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 committee, and the examination procedure applies where Article 98(2) is referenced.
quote: "The Commission shall be assisted by a committee. That committee shall be a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011."
legal_practice_note: This governs implementing acts relevant to AI Act administration.

summary: Member States must set rules on penalties and other enforcement measures for operator infringements and ensure proper and effective implementation.
quote: "Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties and other enforcement measures, which may also include warnings and non-monetary measures, applicable to infringements of this Regulation by operators"
legal_practice_note: Member State penalty rules determine enforcement exposure for legal-AI operators.

summary: Member States must notify the Commission of penalty and enforcement-measure rules by the date of entry into application and of later amendments without delay.
quote: "The Member States shall, without delay and at the latest by the date of entry into application, notify the Commission of the rules on penalties"
legal_practice_note: This is a Member State notification duty.

summary: Non-compliance with Article 5 prohibited AI practices carries administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, for undertakings, up to 7 % of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.
quote: "administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher"
legal_practice_note: This is the highest fine tier and can apply to prohibited AI practices in legal services or courts.

summary: Non-compliance with listed operator, notified-body and Article 50 transparency obligations carries fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or up to 3 % of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.
quote: "administrative fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher"
legal_practice_note: This fine tier can reach legal-AI providers and deployers for listed obligations.

summary: Supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request carries fines of up to EUR 7 500 000 or up to 1 % of worldwide annual turnover.
quote: "administrative fines of up to EUR 7 500 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 1 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI actors responding to authority or notified-body requests face this accuracy-related fine tier.

summary: For SMEs, including startups, each Article 99 fine is capped at the lower of the applicable percentage or amount in Article 99(3), (4) or (5).
quote: "In the case of SMEs, including start-ups, each fine referred to in this Article shall be up to the percentages or amount referred to in paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, whichever thereof is lower."
legal_practice_note: Startup legal-AI vendors may benefit from the SME lower-of cap.

summary: Authorities deciding whether and how much to fine must consider all relevant circumstances, including gravity, turnover, cooperation, responsibility, notification, intent and mitigation.
quote: "all relevant circumstances of the specific situation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: Fine-setting factors are relevant to legal-AI providers, deployers and notified bodies in enforcement.

summary: Each Member State must set rules on the extent to which administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies it establishes.
quote: "Each Member State shall lay down rules on to what extent administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in that Member State."
legal_practice_note: This matters to courts and public legal bodies deploying AI where national law permits fines.

summary: The exercise of penalty powers must be subject to procedural safeguards under Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process.
quote: "The exercise of powers under this Article shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and national law"
legal_practice_note: Legal-AI actors subject to penalties have procedural safeguards and remedies.

summary: Member States must annually report to the Commission on administrative fines issued under Article 99 and related litigation or judicial proceedings.
quote: "Member States shall, on an annual basis, report to the Commission about the administrative fines they have issued during that year"
legal_practice_note: This is a Member State reporting duty about penalty enforcement.

summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor may impose administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies within scope, taking all listed circumstances into account.
quote: "The European Data Protection Supervisor may impose administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies falling within the scope of this Regulation."
legal_practice_note: This covers EU bodies that act as AI providers or deployers, including legal institutions outside judicial exceptions.

summary: Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies that breach Article 5 prohibited practices face administrative fines of up to EUR 1 500 000.
quote: "Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 1 500 000."
legal_practice_note: This may affect EU legal bodies or institutions using prohibited AI practices.

summary: Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies face administrative fines of up to EUR 750 000 for other AI-system requirements or obligations under the Regulation.
quote: "The non-compliance of the AI system with any requirements or obligations under this Regulation, other than those laid down in Article 5, shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 750 000."
legal_practice_note: This can reach EU bodies deploying or providing regulated AI outside Article 5.

summary: Before EDPS fine decisions, the affected Union institution or body must have an opportunity to be heard, complainants must be closely associated, and defence rights and file access must be respected.
quote: "Before taking decisions pursuant to this Article, the European Data Protection Supervisor shall give the Union institution, body, office or agency which is the subject of the proceedings"
legal_practice_note: This sets procedural rights for Union bodies in AI Act fine proceedings.

summary: Funds from Article 100 fines contribute to the Union budget, fines must not affect effective operation of the fined body, and EDPS must notify the Commission annually.
quote: "Funds collected by imposition of fines in this Article shall contribute to the general budget of the Union."
legal_practice_note: This governs disposition and reporting of EDPS fines.

summary: The Commission may fine GPAI model providers up to 3 % of annual total worldwide turnover or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher, for intentional or negligent listed infringements.
quote: "fines not exceeding 3 % of their annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher"
legal_practice_note: This reaches GPAI providers whose models may be integrated into legal AI systems.

summary: Before adopting a GPAI fine decision, the Commission must communicate preliminary findings to the provider and give it an opportunity to be heard.
quote: "the Commission shall communicate its preliminary findings to the provider of the general-purpose AI model and give it an opportunity to be heard"
legal_practice_note: GPAI providers in legal-AI supply chains receive hearing rights before fines.

summary: Fines imposed on GPAI providers under Article 101 must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
quote: "Fines imposed in accordance with this Article shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive."
legal_practice_note: This is the Article 101 fine standard.

summary: Information on Article 101 fines must be communicated to the Board as appropriate, and the Court of Justice has unlimited jurisdiction to review Commission fine decisions.
quote: "The Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions of the Commission fixing a fine under this Article."
legal_practice_note: This provides judicial review for GPAI providers fined under Article 101.

summary: The Commission must adopt implementing acts containing detailed arrangements and procedural safeguards for Article 101 fine proceedings.
quote: "The Commission shall adopt implementing acts containing detailed arrangements and procedural safeguards for proceedings"
legal_practice_note: This governs future procedure for GPAI fine cases.

summary: Article 102 amends Regulation (EC) No 300/2008 so that AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements are taken into account for security equipment concerning Artificial Intelligence systems.
quote: "the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: This sectoral product-law amendment has no direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Article 103 amends Regulation (EU) No 167/2013 so that AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements are taken into account for artificial intelligence systems which are safety components.
quote: "the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: This sectoral product-law amendment has no direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Article 104 amends Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 so that AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements are taken into account for Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components.
quote: "the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: This sectoral product-law amendment has no direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Article 105 amends Directive 2014/90/EU so that AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements are taken into account for Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components.
quote: "the Commission shall take into account the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation"
legal_practice_note: This sectoral product-law amendment has no direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Article 106 amends Directive (EU) 2016/797 so that AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements are taken into account for Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components.
quote: "the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: This sectoral product-law amendment has no direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Article 107 amends Regulation (EU) 2018/858 so that AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements are taken into account for Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components.
quote: "the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: This sectoral product-law amendment has no direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Article 108 amends several parts of Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 so AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements are considered for AI safety components in aviation acts.
quote: "the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: This aviation-sector amendment has no direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Article 109 amends Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 so that AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements are taken into account for artificial intelligence systems which are safety components.
quote: "the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account"
legal_practice_note: This sectoral product-law amendment has no direct legal-practice obligation.

summary: Article 110 amends Directive (EU) 2020/1828 by adding the AI Act to Annex I on representative actions for collective consumer-interest protection.
quote: "In Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828 of the European Parliament and of the Council (58), the following point is added:"
legal_practice_note: Consumer collective-action lawyers may encounter AI Act claims through this amendment.

summary: AI components of Annex X large-scale IT systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 must comply by 31 December 2030, without prejudice to Article 5.
quote: "AI systems which are components of the large-scale IT systems established by the legal acts listed in Annex X that have been placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 shall be brought into compliance with this Regulation by 31 December 2030"
transitional_note: Annex X large-scale IT AI components placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 have until 31 December 2030.
legal_practice_note: This transitional rule mainly affects public large-scale IT systems in freedom, security and justice.

summary: Annex X lists large-scale freedom, security and justice IT systems that receive the Article 111 transitional compliance rule for AI components.
quote: "Schengen Information System"
transitional_note: Annex X systems are tied to the Article 111(1) 31 December 2030 transition.
legal_practice_note: This is mostly relevant to public-sector justice and border-management IT systems.

summary: For other high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2026, the Regulation applies only after significant design changes, while public-authority systems must comply by 2 August 2030.
quote: "this Regulation shall apply to operators of high-risk AI systems, other than the systems referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, that have been placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2026, only if"
transitional_note: Pre-2 August 2026 high-risk systems are covered only upon significant design changes; public-authority high-risk systems must comply by 2 August 2030.
legal_practice_note: This transitional rule matters for courts and public legal bodies already using high-risk AI.

summary: Providers of GPAI models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 must take necessary steps to comply with AI Act obligations by 2 August 2027.
quote: "Providers of general-purpose AI models that have been placed on the market before 2 August 2025 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with the obligations laid down in this Regulation by 2 August 2027."
transitional_note: Pre-2 August 2025 GPAI models must comply by 2 August 2027.
legal_practice_note: Legacy GPAI models used by legal-AI tools receive this transition period.

summary: The Commission must annually assess the need to amend Annex III and Article 5 prohibited-practice lists until the Article 97 delegation period ends, and submit findings to Parliament and Council.
quote: "The Commission shall assess the need for amendment of the list set out in Annex III and of the list of prohibited AI practices laid down in Article 5, once a year"
legal_practice_note: Annex III point 8 and Article 5 changes could materially affect legal-AI providers, courts and deployers.

summary: By 2 August 2028 and every four years thereafter, the Commission must evaluate and report on Annex III headings, Article 50 transparency systems and supervision/governance effectiveness.
quote: "By 2 August 2028 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall evaluate and report to the European Parliament and to the Council"
legal_practice_note: Reviews may change high-risk and transparency categories relevant to legal-sector AI.

summary: By 2 August 2029 and every four years thereafter, the Commission must report on evaluation and review of the Regulation, including enforcement structure and possible need for a Union agency.
quote: "By 2 August 2029 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a report on the evaluation and review of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: This is a general review duty that may affect future AI Act governance.

summary: Article 112 reports must pay specific attention to authority resources, penalties, harmonised standards/common specifications and numbers of new market entrants and SMEs.
quote: "The reports referred to in paragraph 2 shall pay specific attention to the following"
legal_practice_note: Penalty and standards data may affect legal-AI compliance expectations.

summary: By 2 August 2028, the Commission must evaluate the AI Office’s functioning, powers, competences and resources and report to Parliament and Council.
quote: "By 2 August 2028, the Commission shall evaluate the functioning of the AI Office"
legal_practice_note: This affects institutional enforcement capacity rather than direct legal-sector duties.

summary: By 2 August 2028 and every four years thereafter, the Commission must report publicly on standardisation deliverables for energy-efficient GPAI model development and assess whether further measures are needed.
quote: "the Commission shall submit a report on the review of the progress on the development of standardisation deliverables on the energy-efficient development of general-purpose AI models"
legal_practice_note: This is most relevant to GPAI model providers, including models used in legal AI.

summary: By 2 August 2028 and every three years thereafter, the Commission must evaluate the impact and effectiveness of voluntary codes of conduct for non-high-risk AI requirements and sustainability.
quote: "the Commission shall evaluate the impact and effectiveness of voluntary codes of conduct"
legal_practice_note: Voluntary codes may influence legal-sector AI governance for non-high-risk systems.

summary: The Board, Member States and national authorities must provide requested information without undue delay, and the AI Office must develop a participative methodology for evaluating risk levels and list additions.
quote: "the Board, the Member States and national competent authorities shall provide the Commission with information upon its request and without undue delay"
legal_practice_note: Risk-level methodology can affect whether legal AI becomes listed as high-risk or transparency-risk.

summary: The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
quote: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union."
legal_practice_note: This sets the legal entry-into-force date.

summary: Unless a specific Article 113 exception applies, the Regulation applies from 2 August 2026.
quote: "It shall apply from 2 August 2026. However:"
legal_practice_note: This is the general application date for most legal-sector AI obligations.

summary: Chapters I and II, including scope, definitions and prohibited AI practices, apply from 2 February 2025.
quote: "Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025;"
legal_practice_note: Article 5 prohibited-practice rules apply early to legal-sector AI.

summary: Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII, Chapter XII and Article 78 apply from 2 August 2025, except Article 101.
quote: "Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101;"
legal_practice_note: This brings penalties and confidentiality, but not Article 101, into application on 2 August 2025.

summary: Article 6(1) and corresponding obligations apply from 2 August 2027.
quote: "Article 6(1) and the corresponding obligations in this Regulation shall apply from 2 August 2027."
legal_practice_note: This delayed date applies to Annex I product-safety high-risk systems, not Annex III legal AI.
